Quote: wedgie, December 02, 2006 08:37 pm
Heh, well basically when the ninja passes in front of a switch, it turns the switch. So as soon as he is covering one pixel of any outer border of a switch, the switch will be triggered. So usually, to get a switch you will just pass straight through it. But you dont have to pass all the way through it, you can just touch one pixel into it.
So in this particular level, if you were standing next to the switch and then you move towards it, you will trigger the exit switch by touching its very far edge, then you move one pixel inwards and it will trigger the drone door switch, as the other switch is one pixel smaller than the exit switch.

you have to make sure you edge towards the right switch, and not just slide through the whole thing.

Quote: Arachnid, 2006-12-18T07:51:43Z
One half-baked idea that's occurred to me is a friends-based rating system. You indicate who your 'friends' are on NUMA - those you trust - and ratings are calculated individually for you, weighting votes by your friends most highly, followed by votes by their friends, and so on. This has several issues, though, mostly technical:
- Requires implementation of a social networking style 'friends' system.
- There's no single 'leaderboard' people can refer to. You can no longer say you're "in the top 10".
- There'd need to be some default for when you're not logged in, which may just become the current system all over again.
- Since ratings have to be calculated in a fairly involved manner, and will vary for every person that's viewing them, there are potential implications for system load. Calculating a top-rated list would be even worse.

THat would be pretty sweet, but, as you mentioned, the calculations would be endless.

My question is what if you have no friends?

the idea would be to select people you trust, i.e. im pretty sure you would trust kablizzy, for example, so he would be added to your friends list. people like sniper101, however, would not be on that list. at least thats what i understand from it..

#275322 31 2006-12-22T22:16:06Z Spawn of Yanni
Obby already addressed that point, -XRXRXRX-:
Quote: Guest, 2006-12-22T21:26:39Z
My point is perfectly fine. You begin at 2, and go on forever. You begin at 3, go on forever. Both contain and infinite amount of numbers. Yet the magnitude of 2 infinity is greater than 3 infinity because you start with one more number.
You are not able to count to infinity, and that is precisely why he says they both contain an infinite amount of numbers. The situation cannot be compared to a race: in a race, the distance between the two runners is variable, if you pick a point halfway through the race, then yes, the result may not be the same at the end of the race. However, it's different with counting to infinity. There's no variable distance or anything, if you pick any point within this concept of infinity and check how much you have counted from each number you would have always counted one more when counting from 2. Simply because you started at 2, not 3; you started earlier.

#275618 52 2006-12-23T09:22:05Z Spawn of Yanni
Soy wakes up, refreshed, only to find that Neil is now asleep, and the strange man is no longer in sight. Realising he would need more than an iKnife, a note, and a midget to help him survive in this island, he decides to get up and explore.

To start with, he looks around this room he was in. Potions. He walks up to one of the shelves that caught his attention, as it was the only one where a bottle is missing. Next to the space is one labelled "Brains of the Buffalo". It didn't take long for Soy to convince himself that drinking this mysterious potion is his destiny. So he drinks the whole thing.

There is an immediate effect. He can see everything so much clearer now, everything is so much sharper to him. He can also tell he had an increased sense of hearing, as all the noises in the room became amplified. The note his father had left him is now a red cloth with the writing still on it (to Soy's relief, the colour didn't cause him to charge towards it head first) and his iKnife has become a sharp tusk-like thing. It is now an iHorn. Thankfully, there were no horns on Soy's head; he is still human on the outside.

Soy decides to go back to Neil, as enough exploring had been done. Finding Neil is a lot easier with his improved sight. When he tried to run back to his spot, he found himself running much faster than he thought he was capable of before.

#282062 12 2007-01-06T18:56:32Z Spawn of Yanni
Clicking every frame? Not sure what you mean by that (maybe something I don't know about) but what I do know is that, in debug mode, you have to have CAPS LOCK on to play the levels. So, when you're at the debug menu, you can press [P] to get the level ready, then turn on caps lock which allows you to actually play through it. You could also switch caps lock on first, and then press [P] to play the level.

When playing a level in debug mode, you can do some extra stuff, too. If you die, you can press [enter] and the ninja will respawn where your cursor is. Also, when you die, you can press [spacebar] to toggle between having your ninja in one piece and exploded, and can hold [shift] and move your mouse around to move the ninja around after he's dead (this also works when he's exploded). Have fun!

While I do see where some people come from when they say it's only fair that Iran has nuclear weapons as well, I personally don't think they should. No emphasis on "they" - I'm saying that, really, no one should be getting anymore nuclear weapons. 1960...something....I'm thinking 1961 or '62 saw the Cuban Missile Crisis where the world was basically on the brink of nuclear war just because the superpowers both had intense nuclear arsenals, Mutually Assured Destruction and all that. That really can't happen again. If Iran already had nuclear weapons by now, the British sailor situation would have been a lot more dangerous - particularly for poor old countries like Bahrain (sob story) who are close to Iran and would basically perish if such a war was to break out. #311344 150 2007-04-08T19:45:01Z Spawn of Yanni
Splash.

Rain. Straight on his face. For the first time in over two months, Soy opens his eyes.

Once he has completely regained conciousness, he tries to to remember his last actions. Running through the forest really fast...seeing random figures trying to use some kind of knife....the tree...

Ah yes. The tree. That tree that seemed to appear magically in front of his face. To be more precise, that grew from a weed to an all-out tree in a couple of seconds. Soy looks in front of him. The tree was no longer there.

Neither were the clothes on his body.

Up ahead, Soy sees a ragged shirt, some dirty jeans, sandals and a brand new set of underwear. He picks them up and wears them, realising that he had now lost all of the equipment he had before - if he could even remember what it was he had.

Were the other people he met still alive? Where were they? Where was he? Why was this rain making unusual holes in his skin?

Soy runs off into a nearby cave for shelter from the seemingly corrosive substance.

#319492 2 2007-05-08T15:02:13Z Spawn of Yanni
Framerate. It stands for milliseconds per frame - the number of milliseconds that each frame exists for. Each frame put together makes a moving image - you know, like how if you draw loads of images of a man walking in slightly different postions in the corner of each page of a book and flip through the pages, it looks like the man is moving? Each page would equal a frame, and this refers to how much time each 'page' is visible to the eye.

You would normally like to keep that number small - the faster the framerate, the better the gameplay seems to be, generally. I think it's usually 8 ms/f, for me at least.

#325396 21 2007-05-29T17:49:24Z Spawn of Yanni
Those games, such as Worms, are very different from N. For one, they have MUCH larger playing arenas. Which means that even randomly generated maps are guaranteed to be playable, since they have a lot of free space. N doesn't have that much space to begin with.

Also, N is far more complex in terms of contents of a map. A randomly generated map refers only to terrain being created. In N, as well as having ground being created, you need to have a ninja, a door and a key to even make it playable. So when randomly generating a map, you need to hope that none of those things end up inside the ground, or that the key or door don't end up in an area in which the ninja can't enter.

Furthermore, even if the door and key are in space, they might be right next to the ninja, which won't make for a very enjoyable map. In addition to all this, there are enemies to be placed if you want to have a decent map. These can also end up in the ground or in an area in which they have no chance of killing the ninja. And, finally, you can't even consider having doors and such, because chances are they will just end up somewhere in the air. So, I'm for the random map selector, but no map generator, thank you very much.

I didn't want to go down the "this is unnecessary" road, because I kind of see that as a poor reason for a suggestion not to be considered. Anyway, when apg suggested this, I saw it more as an opportunity for mapmakers to add a new dimension to their levels. Sure, there could be someone who decides to be an ass and makes a level that can't be all-golded, but what the hell? That's just a stupid map then, isn't it? You don't have to play it. This idea would add a new level of playing to those who play it, as well. A truly good map using this type of door would challenge the player to get all the gold, and if the player doesn't want to get all the gold, well then don't play the level! It's like saying "I don't want to reach the end of MTI, I just want to pass it." A level using this door would have been properly made to challenge as well as entertain the player, unlike the example shown by Ad. His point would be the equivalent of someone posting a map where the ninja starts off on a mine and blows up immediately in a thread where someone suggested that mines be added into the game. Sure, a n00b map can make this suggestion look bad, but a n00b map can make anything look bad, really. Furthermo-

...In-post edit: I just realised that you can do this exact same thing by having a load of locked doors before the exit, so that the player needs to get all the keys. Not quite exactly the same, because it would mean that the door would have to be in some sort of corridor, but it's somewhat the same. Bah. There goes my arguement.

#329134 7 2007-06-09T11:16:19Z Spawn of Yanni
Phase 1: It begins. [Yes this summary is going to have weird-ass phase names. Deal with it.]


The sigs of nevermore, wedgie, Kablizzy, LV, Trogdor, and thecalcgenius had links leading to some parole numeri page. From the corresponding numbers, we got COFFEE - the name of our target.

Trogdor posted another clue identifying the prize again - pointing out the forum we have to get to is #54.




Phase 2: Cerebrum, or Tumbling Down The Rabbit Hole.


"It may go through more than just space."

Trog keeps hinting at time and the future. Look at the last day in the calendar (without editing the address) and you get an entry called Cerebrum.

Searching cerebrum gives you a post by Trogdor that mentions the Noetic Realm, which fits in the asterisks in the calendar entry.

Forum searching Noetic Realm gave us the clue to search for the man of the mind (enter stupidity by me here).

The man of the mind is a member called Cerebrum.

Cerebrum's signature has links to various members, do some funky shit here with the third character of each name and you get CHITS. CHIT is a word that is found in another link in his sig.

The first letter is found here: S, from the difference mentioned above.




Phase 3: Enter the Mafia.


Forum searching CHIT gives you a nevermore post."I am surrounded by noise. It's time to enlist in La Cosa Nostra. Are you ready?"

"I am surrounded by noise" gives you the second letter: I - This is the tricky one. Trog already confirmed that this is the right letter, but said we haven't found it the right way. My theory is that it refers to the "I" itself being surrounded by letters in the word "noise". I am probably wrong.

La Cosa Nostra is the Mafia. So we must join the mafia, i.e. check out the mafia joining thread.

At the end of the first post in this thread is the edit "3/1/1 - LETTER MAFIOSO MAFIA" with the slashes going to http://ntoysmmosef/ and http://of.the.18th.server.forumer/

This gives us 3rd Letter, 1st Mafioso, 1st Mafia: In the first game of Mafia on the forums, IangB was the first mafioso: so the letter must be N.

In that same thread, there is also a clue at the bottom of the first post giving us the letter E, after some cool maths shit.




Phase 4: Shit, It's Brit.


Shift the letters ntoysmmosef one space to the left and you get BritanniaWD. With the clue "of the 18th forumer", we are sent to britanniawd.18.forumer.com.

There, a thread by Brit is found. It tells us the next letter is N, and leads us to the 75th thing that you can't post in suggestions in another thread here on metanet.

The 75th thing is a samurai, with a reference to the letter S. This is where we hit the bottom of the rabbit hole. We have the letters SINENS.



Phase 5: Into the Dragon's Den.


Brit's sig on the other forum completes the set of sigs from all the players. Taking the underlined letters from each of their sigs gives us NAAGGOY, or, rearranged, ANAGOGY.

Forum searching ANAGOGY gives us a Brit post: "Welcome to the Dragon's Den. ANAGOGY."

Forum searching Dragon's Den (or doing some exceedingly cool but useless "Hell" shit) gives you another Brit post.

A link at the end of the Brit post gives us the letter A, seemingly the first of this new word.

"123: "this is the first ever map ive made, im still not totally sure how to use teleports or how to make the \\\'smoke\\\' type explosion thingy. anyone care to comment?" <-This refers to a map description by wedgie123 (wedgie on NUMA).

Search this on Google, and you get a cached result of his map. The description has since been changed, to "Dragon's Den. My first, it goes upside down." Take wedgie's first letter, turn it upside down, you get the second letter: M.



Phase 6: SeXy.


The most recent comment on the map is by nevermore, telling us to find what wedgie has to say about the X, on Friday 13th 2005.

On that date, wedgie made a post in a nevermore thread referring to a map called "Unlocking the X". At the end of his post is "Mhm. Another clue pending."

The "e" in that clue is in italics, suggesting that the next letter is E.

A while later, the "Another clue pending" changes to "#Nottherabbithole", a clear reference to an IRC channel.



Phase 7: You said there was no IRC! ;_;


Going to the channel #DragonDen gets you immediately kicked from it. However, it gives the message - "Hey, I didn't invite you into this! Chanserv attack! By the by, the next two letters are L. Sic!"

So, we have the next two letters, L and L.

Forum searching "Sic" gives you a thecalcgenius post with this clue: "Chanserv sic! Retrospect, and look at the beginning of the Dragon's Den. See it. Listen, too. See it."

"See" is underlined. This is a clue referring to the letter C. However, it's not as simple as that. TCG is telling us to go back to the beginning of the Dragon's Den - GASP! That means C is actually the FIRST letter of this new word.



Phase 8: Fuck, how many phases are there?


Just when it seems there are no leads to follow, the very first post of the thread has been edited. "Welcome to the end. Dragon's Den: IA. Rabbit Hole: IS."

This means that we should add these letters to the ends of the words they refer to. For the first phase, the Rabbit Hole, we had SINENS. Add IS to the end, and we come up with SINENSIS.

For the Dragon's Den, we have CAMELL. Add IA to the end, and we come up with CAMELLIA.

Trog previously mentioned that the words don't necessarily go in the order we found them. So it's not SINENSIS CAMELLIA, it's CAMELLIA SINENSIS.

Camellia Sinensis is some sort of Green Tea - Kamikaze, when he was accepted into your ranks, made references of Green Tea, confirming the significance of Camellia Sinensis.

And that's it. The password. Here I am. It's been fun.

#333938 45 2007-06-21T11:40:15Z Spawn of Yanni
usaswim: SIGATARS
xaelar

Design - 9/10 <- Pretty darn sweet design. Seems a bit empty in the middle.
Theme - 3/5 <- A bit scattered, I would have preferred it if you stuck with the flowy theme of the left side.
Flow - 8/10 <- The colours go very well; the background, though, doesn't quite go with the foreground.
Avatar - 5/5
Overall look - 18/20 <- You've got a nice sigatar set here. It could have come out better, though, with a different background, I feel.
Total - 43/50
Nice style you have here. /me likes.

CDotLeach

Design - 7/10 <- Very nice central section. That sig is begging for a transparent background.
Theme - 5/5 <- Yeppideedoodah.
Flow - 8/10 <- The text and the middle go together very well; the lines in the foreground...I don't know. A little distracting, while it fits at the same time. Not sure what to say about them.
Avatar - 5/5 <- I should see a movie this weekend. Shrek 3? Hmm, maybe. For some reason it doesn't interest me too much.
Overall look - 17/20 <- The white background takes away from the overall look. The middle section is brilliantly done. Another little note; try not to get too repetitve in terms of colours.

Total - 42/50
The colours are what bothers me about this. Don't conform to the blue-and-white-ness.

LARGE SIG

Blue Ray: (GAH! southpaw! Link to his profile for this one, it's four different images! I'm judging his actual sig, from his profile. No worries, 'swim.)

Colors - 11/15 <- The...the...THE BLUE AND WHITE! Not only that, but the blue is a little too light for me. You should have made it deeper if you're using this colour scheme, similar to the CDot one.
Theme - 3/5 <- Meh. Very much all over the place. Seems like you tried to do too much in this one.
Design - 13/15 <- I do not like the colours, or the messy right side of this one. However, this is where I would judge the genius that is the split-image-linking-ness. It's brilliantly done, you can't tell that it's a split image, and just....well done.
Overall look - 12/15 <- Unfortunately, the split image usage can't be judged here - pretty much the best aspect of that sig. I'm not a fan of the look of this sig, it generally seems a bit...messy.

Total - 39/50
Not your best work. Still, one can't say it looks bad, it just needs some sort of central idea.


10tacle: SIGATAR
Halo 2

Design - 6/10 <- A little hard to see what's going on at first. Needs a border. Still, I rather like the subtle change of colours.
Theme - 5/5 <- No, I can't see a theme here. I'm also blind.
Flow - 8/10 <- Y'know, it does actually go together pretty well. The font used for your name is great. The Halo 2 logo could maybe have fit in a little more with the subtle theme of the rest of the sig.
Avatar - 3/5 <- Yes, it's still Halo, but looking at them both, it's a very drastic change from signature to avatar. Especially the colour - shouldn't have had white in the avatar.
Overall look - 16/20 <- While in separate components this may seem a very good sig, on the whole, it just doesn't seem too appealing.

Total - 38/50
It's alright. Submitting it as a sigatar set wasn't a great idea, not with that avatar. It needs to look a lot more like the sig.


And that's my judging marathon over for today.

Mare and Raigan specifically said that multiplayer should not be suggested for the next version of N for the PC. It's not just about a disliking of the idea, it's just that it's not entirely possible for them to implement it using Flash, as well as the fact that they'd have to change a lot of the gameplay to suit multiplayer. Now with N+, which is coming out on platforms which do support multiplayer, they have decided to include it because essentially they're starting from scratch, meaning that they can make the game with the idea of multiplayer in their heads. No doubt multiplayer will be something to look forward to, which is why everyone is "drooling over it". The message at the top of the suggestions forum has been put there at M&R's request, I believe, because those are elements they simply do not want in the PC N. N+ is going to be something completely different.

#354644 3 2007-08-12T23:29:39Z Spawn of Yanni
Post count doesn't mean anything. I can think of so many non-metanember members who easily deserve the title more than certain other people who are metanembers. I can't even begin to tell you how little talent I have when it comes to maps, so don't worry about that. Several members who have custom titles right now actually asked for them, something which I find pretty strange to do, because it really won't mean as much that way.

Don't watch over your topics like a hawk; don't prepare to be judged by them. Topics aren't maps - there's a reason why I was against that "topic rating" system someone suggested a while back, the reason being exactly this. Don't make a topic in the hope that someone will see it and immediately give you +50 respect points, make a topic if you think that others will actually find it interesting. I don't actually take much notice of the person posting the topic, I just read what they have to say.

I guess the point that would cover most of your other problems would be - don't try so damn hard, man. This place is just like any group of friends. You can imagine the one guy who's always cracking the cheesy jokes and raising his hand in the hope of a high-five, while everyone else just sees him as a freak. I'm not saying that's who you are, I'm saying that's who you could become if you keep trying to 'be cool' and all that. I used to try real hard to fit in. It really didn't work. Being myself has done me pretty good around here, if I may say so myself.

And then again, who am I to say all this? I've not even been here for a year yet. You've got to think about what you think of yourself, really.

Of course, you're bound to get noticed by hanging around a lot. Nothing to do with post count, a lot to do with contributing. Find something to do. I chose comics. A large majority of members chose imaging. Some go for coding. Find something, anything, you're even mildly good at, and work on that. Hell, show it off.

Oh, and the N IRC channel is a great place to chat with a lot of the forum members. You should hang around there.

#369796 4 2007-10-05T07:01:50Z Spawn of Yanni
Indian soap operas are far more dramatic than any other soap operas I've seen. The camera work is ridiculous. To emphasise an event, the camera would, for example, zoom in on the main character's face, three times. It would then do a rapid pan of the room he's in, zooming into him some more during this, and then have the camera move so that his face comes in three times from the left, three times from the right, and then zoom in to his face three times again. In an especially dramatic scene, the camera would then proceed to do some twists, and all previous camera movements would have a bit of a trail on. If the scene in question deals with more than one person dealing with shock as a result of the dramatic event that has just taken place, this whole process is repeated for the next person. It looks like the director has just bought some video editing program and is playing with the features. As in, seriously.

But hey, that's what Indian drama is. Drama. To the max. They really don't hold back. And there's no reason for them not to - Indian cinema is Indian cinema, this is what they do. There's no reason for them to be like Hollywood or anything.

#379399 243 2007-11-14T13:52:29Z Spawn of Yanni
Well, if the two columns represent two different functions being applied to two operands to get a result (which is what I initially thought, put in doubt by the Wingdings thing), then those functions aren't simple functions. That is, they aren't a single operator (addition, subtraction, multiplication or division). The bottom-left thingo, with the two three-dots resulting in two squares, represents something happening to two identical digits to get an answer with two other identical digits. No single operator can do this - not even raising to the power of, at least not when the two operands are the same.

Basically, if we're going down a maths route, we could be looking at multiplying the first by the second and then adding a number - things along those lines. xy + 2, 5x + y, etc.

Oh, one more thing. I'm working under the assumption that the two operands are the left digit and the top digit, and the result is the other bit (for the left column). For the right column, I'm seeing it as the two top bits are operands, and the bottom bit is the result. It doesn't have to be this way.

The bottom-left and the third one down both look very similar in terms of organisation. To an extent, so do the second one down and the fourth one down. We have to think about that when trying to figure out what the relationships are.

Dave said "The symbols are another language. The images are digits." Lenny interpreted this as the ~ and stuff are the symbols, and the squares and triangles are digits. I didn't think of that, actually. I assumed he meant all ~s and three-dots and squares etc were images, while those lines between them (the relationships) were the symbols. I took this 'other language' to be maths. Now that I think of it, though, Lenny could well be right. Hummm. We need to split them into symbols and images if he is, though, to make sure we look at this the right way.

Dave also originally presented the puzzle as "The locks" and "The keys". Perhaps one of these columns will help us with the other? If so, I get the feeling it's the right one, for some reason. But hey, maybe not.

So, yeah, that's my input.

/me disappears.

"OH GOD JESUS M********* SAVE ME" squealed Dave, as he hid behind Chuck.

"Oh, someone's getting hurt, whether you like it or not" replied Chuck. With one swift motion, his left leg swung around as he spun on his right heel and unleashed a deadly blow onto Amy's unsuspecting face.

#380183 14 2007-11-17T15:30:01Z Spawn of Yanni
*The Next Day*




Sally awoke with a start. She had just had that nightmare again. The journey in her car; the mysterious man in the passenger seat; "It's coming to an end," he had said (she could never forget those foreboding words); the sudden shower of...

Her mind snapped back to the present. Day dreaming wasn't going to get the house cleaned. For the first time that day, she looked around and took in what she saw, sparking memories of the events of the day before.

The remains of the rat were still splattered all over the walls. She expected nothing less; Chuck wasn't the type to clean up his mess.

"The poor thing could've never seen it coming", she said, to no one in particular. Wondering where Chuck and Dave were, she went to the kitchen to make herself some food before the daunting task of cleaning up the rat. On the table was a note.

"Tired of world. Leaving on rat's escape pod. Love you."

The note was signed "Chuck". The question that immediately cropped up in her head was answered when she turned the note over and saw "I'm off too. Dave." Annoyed, she scrunched up the note and through it in the bin, wondering why they didn't take her with them. She noticed that she didn't hear the satisfying sound of paper hitting the side of a bin as it dropped in. She looked around to see that her bin was gone.

"B*******. They took my bin." She was rather attatched to that bin. It provided her shelter for 7 months in 1982. Still, she had to keep moving. The house needed cleaning, and the bin needed replacing. She decided to start with the latter.

Relieved to find that Chuck and Dave hadn't somehow taken her car, she put her keys in the ignition and started up. She loved driving. It seemed to be as close as she could get to getting away from the rest of the world. Cruising at 60 miles per hour on the freeway, Sally noticed that on her right was a disturbingly long line of... what were they? She slowed down and moved into the right lane, wanting to find out more, and immediately regretted her decision.

Not 4 seconds after her action, Sally's car was surrounded by the mysterious walkers. Left, right, front, back, on top of - even a couple underneath, but then their faces were underneath the tires, so they posed no serious threat. Amongst the chaos came one man, who Sally noticed was actually fighting people off her car. Did he want her for himself? Or was he really trying to save her? His face was pressed against the windscreen now, and she could see him mouthing "DRIVE DRIVE DRIVE B****!" She pressed down hard on the pedal, and the swarm of attackers were helpless as they fell by the sides of the car. Only one remained - her apparent saviour. She stopped, and let him in - an action that she really didn't understand, only justified by the fact that she didn't understand anything that was going on anyway.

"Thank you, ma'am." Sally looked at him and wondered why she was being thanked. She opened her mouth to thank him, but he stopped her. "Please. Just... thank you."

A few minutes passed, and they were getting to know each other. Sally had just established that he was a huge fan of Lost - her favourite show.

"You love it too?" he asked Sally, as she nodded. "Oh, it's wonderful," he continued. "This season is easily the best. It's a pity, though," he said with a chuckle.

"A pity? What do you mean?" she asked.

"You know. It's coming to an end."

Sally's heart skipped about seven beats.

She looked to the sky.

"Oh my God."

#386604 2 2007-12-05T15:51:21Z Spawn of Yanni
I'd like to say that procrastination is a huge problem of mine, but the fact is that it's not been as bad for me as it has for you. That said, I do have problems with getting down to work. My GCSE results suffered because I was on here too much; while they weren't bad, by any means, they were nowhere near what I would've liked. I feel my first shot at SAT 1 may have also been affected by the forums, but perhaps not as badly - the GCSEs were something of a wake-up call, and my priorities are somewhat clearer to me now.

All this, of course, doesn't affect you... what I wanted to say was that I've always had a problem of not being able to get down to work - I set myself early deadlines, and then simply push them back, one hour at a time, thinking it won't make any difference. What I've found that helps me get down to it is to make the work enjoyable. I'm always using up my work time to play games, so I figured if I make the work more enjoyable, then I won't be trying to postpone it by doing other stuff. There's only one way, for me, that makes homework/coursework enjoyable.

That's got to be music. Not just on speakers somewhere in the room, but with headphones, straight into my ears. It blocks everything else out, and at the right volume, it allows me to think straight at the same time. Occasionally, I find that the music will be distracting me from the work. At such times, I'll just stop and take a break. There's no good trying to get back into that work mood when I've been thrown out of it, that never works for me. But with music as an incentive, I've found that it isn't anywhere as hard to get started on work. This, though, is what works for me. I'm a music guy; guitar is my life, and I can fall pretty deep into some songs. Simply listening to music I like is a fun activity, which makes it the perfect method of overcoming my procrastination. I have no idea if it'll work for you... I guess you'll have to find out what does. Something that'll make you think "Damnit, work. At least I have this as well."


Well, music is the only thing I can think of.


Edit: There's one other thing that helps me do stuff that I know I'm going to delay, and that's catching myself by surprise. While saying "Nahhh, I'll do it later", I might simply walk over to my desk, take out some books, and start work. The idea is that I don't have time to think about what I'm doing, and once I've gotten started, I can get down to doing it. This works for pretty much anything, for me - talking to... certain people; going to the gym; even waking up. Just jump out of bed, y'know? Doing things without a second thought.

#388360 10 2007-12-11T16:24:10Z Spawn of Yanni
Well, celebrities got where they are by dedicating themselves to doing what they do. They got there thanks to a degree of hard work and commitment, and to say they don't deserve the money... well, it'd be unfair to say that. You can't really know if they really deserve it or not.

You say that there's no reason we should care about their lives. Take a celebrity having a baby; of course, there are millions around the world who would've had a baby on the same day, but the difference is that these are, quite simply, people we are familiar with. We don't know who Parvita Krishnamuralitharan is, but we do know Halle Berry. We've seen her in movies, so she's a familiar face. Immediately, that makes any news about her relevant. In the same way I would care if that kid in Year 7 got into a fight, I would care if Britney Spears decided model her head as a bowling ball. I recognise the name, and that familiarity makes the news interesting/entertaining.

The other thing about celebrity news is that it lets us in to the part of their lives that we never get to see. We usually only see the screen personalities. While Jack Bauer is out stopping terrorists, Kiefer's gettin' wasted. I can understand how you might disagree, but I simply find that interesting to know - seeing the human faces behind the light and make-up.

Why do you see these people so often in the news? The public -wants- to know. The large majority, that is. You said it yourself, all your friends at school find the news interesting. The people who print these stories, they're the ones who benefit from them. If one kid out of every thousand says "Who gives a damn!?", they will really not care. They'll still be raking in the money. By -making- the stories sound large and grand, they make people want to read about them. More readers = more money. Tha's what it's all about, these days.

McP3000
=======
McP3000 was banned for making a death threat towards Arona Daal, on top of several other infractions which had previously resulted in him being suspended. Seeing as he only just returned from a suspension, the staff decided that this was it for old McP.

Arona Daal made the thread I hate in Bash & Thrash, intended to let people tell others what they hate in the world. While it may not have been the most intelligent topic to grace these forums, McP's post was unwarranted and unnecessary - as a death threat always is, no matter what the context. This, on top of McP's existing warn log - which was "one of the most entertaining things I've read in a while" (according to Tsukatu) - proved to be too much.

Examples of other offences include posting a picture in Serious Discussion who's subject was "Buttsecks". He then did it again after it was taken down. He was suspended for this because he obviously knew better. Not long after the suspension was lifted, he made this death threat - after a suspension, you pretty much have to be perfect. Death threats aren't perfect.

Pros: He wasn't really an idiot as such; to some extent, he was a respected member of the forums.
Cons: Huge repeat offender. Bobby Brown ain't got nothin' on him.

Morals:
  • No death threats. Ever. Anywhere. It is very possible you will get banned.
  • Lots of warns =/= good thing. Try staying away from them; I hear it helps.

#396184 2 2008-01-03T13:41:40Z Spawn of Yanni
The time you start with at the beginning of each level depends on the time you've spent on the previous levels in the episode. You start and episode with 90 seconds on the clock, and the time remaining at the end of that first level will be the time you start with at the beginning of the next level of the episode.

Basically, if you find yourself with only six seconds left on the clock, you'll probably have to try the episode again, except taking less time on the first levels.

#418414 2 2008-03-18T16:40:19Z Spawn of Yanni
Above your right, left, up, and down arrow keys, there should be a bunch of keys like Delete, Insert, Page Up, Page Down, End, and Home. The last one, Home, is the one you're looking for.

If you're on a laptop, try looking for the Home key near the right of the keyboard, it should be in a different colour from most of the other keys. Press "Function" and then that key.
#418418 4 2008-03-18T16:52:59Z Spawn of Yanni
It's not really a coloured key, it's just that the text will be a different colour.

Like:

If, for example, the Home key was the same as your right arrow key, the right arrow would be in white, and the text "Home" would be in blue. You would have to press "Function" and then the right arrow key to get "Home".

Find your Function key; whatever colour the "Function" text is in, that should be the colour the text of "Home" is in. Look for "Home" in that colour around the keyboard.
#418421 6 2008-03-18T17:00:00Z Spawn of Yanni
Hold on, it might not even be a function-combination key thing.

Look at this pic: http://www.notebookreview.com/assets/2013.jpg

The Home key is in the top right. What I said in my last post, I was talking about how the "Pause" button is the same as the Home button, but the "Pause" text is the same colour as the Function key. The difference in the pic is that you don't have to press Function to get to Home.

So, check for those different coloured texts, but also check to see if it might be a key on its own, maybe in the top right or something.


Also, see how in that pic there's a Home key hidden as a function-combination of the "7" key? Check for things like that, too.

#21274 1 2008-08-28T13:47:43Z Spawn of Yanni
The new post on the Numa home page got me thinking - Hot Maps is essentially now being officially recognised as a replacement for the old "Newest Maps" page. I still firmly believe that Active Authors would be a better replacement, as long as you allow the user to go beyond just the 10 newest authors (by saying "Next 10" at the bottom or something, you know what I mean). The Active Authors page, I thought, was pretty fantastic when it first came out, since it was a great way of showing loads of new maps, and there was no need to worry about getting the page flooded by one author.

In my opinion, Active Authors should be the first page you see when you click on the Maps tab. I think most people took Hot Maps as the new Newest Maps page because it's the first thing you see after clicking Maps. (I'm assuming that Hot Maps wasn't -meant- to be the Newest Maps replacement, higher-ups correct me if I'm wrong.)

At the same time, if Active Authors is going to be serve as the Newest Maps page, whatever formula currently makes the Hot Maps page look how it does needs to be reworked. I first thought it was based on Dave's Float and Sink idea, but either it isn't, or it is based on that and the idea isn't working. It should really be doing what I feel it was first made to do, and what its name would suggest - creating a "top-rated of the moment" sort of list. I'm not sure exactly how it would work, perhaps some kind of weekly top-rated list or something.

Currently, the Active Authors page is almost entirely useless. As far as I know, no one seems to be using it. Instead, what we have is a sort of screwy new maps page in Hot Maps.

#470507 81 2008-09-16T13:25:39Z Spawn of Yanni
I played N+ PSP today, and after reading the complaints here, I was really impressed with the game. The bounce blocks, yeah. I tried not to do quick jumps off of them most of the time, which toned down the frustration a bit there.

I loved the PSP running animations. Also the subtle shifting of the screen as you move around. The response to jumping off slanted surfaces was also far better than it is in N. Some of the level designs were fantastic, and provided that same kind of "AAH SCREW THIS BUT I STILL WANT TO FINISH THE GAME" feeling I got when playing the original. The level selection screen is odd, but innovative. I was rather fond of it. The animation for dying from a fall, though, was pretty bad. Nothing to cry about.

Graphics-wise, I wasn't horrified or anything. Quite often I can't make out what enemy is in a level - I thought the chaingun drone was a glitched laser drone for a long time until I actually came across a laser drone. Still, the menus sorta get you ready for the change in graphical style, and I really saw little wrong with it.

I could easily play this game for a long time. That is, if I actually had my own PSP and was playing on that, and not a friend's. ;_;

#475229 3 2008-10-16T13:04:04Z Spawn of Yanni
Quote: OrigamiGuy, December 25, 2007 08:42 pm
Try this; it worked for me.


The problem comes from Vista trying to meld your system sounds together and add audio enhancements, which is why moving N to a lower place in the sound queue sometimes works. Maratanos's solution of disabling the sound output will also work.

But I needed sound effects for running my ninja around; sometimes I just want to hear the little guy explode. Here's what I did:

1.) Go to Start => Control Panel => Sound.
2.) On the Playback tab, right-click your speakers on the list there and select "Properties".
3.) Depending on your speaker setup and your version of Vista, there should be a tab there called "Effects" or "Enhancements" or some such. Check the box marked "Disable System Effects" or "Disable All Enhancements" or whatever.
4.) Play N lag-free!

I hope this works for you as well as it did for me. Enjoy!
This seems to work for most people.
